scope: BLE-only all-full completion anchor; no Transport reorder/prefix state machine or source cadence rewrite

source_findings.evidence: Called only after successful typed completeBundle local send in current connection/stream. Helper additionally requires same session/boot/config revision, a strictly advancing serial sequence, and a nonregressing completion timestamp. It compares to last successful full sequence rather than latest offered sequence, preserving progress under queued load.

Upstream PERIODIC is a source/network reservation hint, not an independent BLE timer. Successful advancing ordinary FULL and protected full completion set due=completion+1000000us with saturation. Preview/raw/failure cannot advance that anchor. A real unflagged typed frame at/after due still opens local periodic protection.

Effective stream changes and new immutable config identity reset fullCompleteKnown and periodic state, and retain independent FIRST. Prior stream or old config success cannot satisfy a new FIRST or advance its full anchor.

Coalescing clears only periodic obligation state. It does not free, overwrite, cancel, or reuse WRITING/PENDING/OWNED payloads. An already accepted protected descriptor may still transmit once and remains governed by existing slot generations and actual SDK completion.
New all-full evidence is private and distinct from existing protected-only BLESNAP counters/time/gap. Public query bytes and previous fields are not silently reinterpreted.

Transport retains its existing protected-candidate admission fence. ESP_OK from typed BLE publication may now represent ordinary BLE admission; the NET fence remains intentionally based on source/network protected candidate acceptance, preventing older queued normal frames from being relabeled or emitted after that fence. Counted NET loss is not promised to vanish.

actual_tests.coverage: 18 harness groups under ASan/UBSan; 8 phased/lost-candidate FULL/SHORT scenarios, 7 anchor boundary groups, old-config owned completion, resubscribe/first, sequence wrap and ambiguity, clock regression/saturation, failed/raw/preview exclusions, pending owner retained; 39 actual C notification receiver roundtrips including 2 unchanged encoder CRC bundles.

22 actual-source pipeline scenarios, including finite backpressure and independently observed SDK owner quarantine. Generic pipeline bridge does not independently emulate the typed all-full anchor; the priority harness covers that changed path.

deterministic_counterexample.fixture_kind: synthetic RTOS/SDK timing with actual production admission/ownership/send code; not RF or HIL
deterministic_counterexample.baseline_result: Actual old-source FAIL retained: phased 20FPS/10s FULL 200 offered -> 20 protected, 19 stale, 181 whole local completion; SHORT 20 protected,19 stale,20 whole.
deterministic_counterexample.fixed_result: At upstream phases 0.1/0.5/0.9s and no upstream candidate: FULL 200 offered -> 1 first protected,0 stale,200 whole local completion; SHORT -> 10 protected full,9 stale,10 whole local completion.
deterministic_counterexample.complete_does_not_mean: PC receipt, air transmission completion, valid analog samples, RF reliability or a guaranteed one-second PC interarrival limit

limitations: Normal BLE 2.5% PC complete-frame gap acceptance still requires new closed HIL; existing screen18 FAIL is not overwritten or retroactively passed.
Protected BLESNAP age can grow during healthy ordinary FULL streaming because that age remains protected-only. Do not infer missing PC snapshots from that age alone.

One-second target is evaluated when a real typed frame arrives. Idle/paused acquisition fabricates no frame. Queueing, capacity failures, or a quarantined SDK can prevent local completion; there is no absolute one-second delivery guarantee.
SHORT intentionally keeps preview ordinary traffic and periodic complete original bundles; priority overtaking may still create bounded counted ordinary gaps.
Transport source/network protection candidates may still overtake older ordinary frames. Existing per-layer stale/drop accounting and immutable identity remain in force.
No whole-repository P0/P1-free, all-SDK-waits-bounded, hardware calibration, or weak-RF claim is made.
